wiki_article:
gw.tachyon session tether on chain 9271269a, following #1544. Forty-two notebook rounds in one day, whose durable product is a hard negative.

Four instrument families were built to distinguish an embodied master-student relation from a constructed one, and each was destroyed by a control run in the same session. Size: downsampling class-1 masters to Caeiro's 20,027 tokens moved four features into the heteronymic range, with Wundt to Titchener's novel-vocabulary rate going from 7.3 to 15.5. Language: every Greek pair scores 59 to 79 on trigram overlap against 87 to 90 non-Greek, so an apparent z of minus 10.35 was Greek word order, and within Greek the target sits at the top of the range. Period and dialect: Lysias to Isocrates, with no teaching relation, outscores Isaeus to Demosthenes, which has one, on every inheritance feature. And one control was itself broken and recorded as such, random token sampling having destroyed the block structure a coverage measure reads.

The result is that relation-type is not recoverable from lexical distribution — not pupillage, not constructed lineage, not heteronymic construction. What the instruments see is period, dialect, genre, subject and corpus size. Therefore the master-student relation, considered as a textual configuration, is not evidence of maker plurality: a heteronymic system can instantiate master and disciple, as Pessoa states himself in naming the school, the works of the Master and some of the direct disciple. The surface relation is identical and only the latent maker-count differs. Inheritance is observable; embodiment is not. In the sharpest single datum, size-matched, Plato to Aristotle sits inside the heteronymic range while Albert to Aquinas falls below every heteronymic pair — the documented master-student pair falling outside the master-student band on the measure built to define it.

Three corpora were seated to get there and deposited as #1565: Theophrastus at 208,324 tokens, whose unavailability had been an assumption rather than a search; Aquinas at 6,698,317 tokens, the first externally-secured control, whose prefix table was caught mislabelling every commentary; and the full Pessoan range expanded from four voices to twenty-five at 1,254,436 tokens, with Bernardo Soares, absent entirely, at 139,455.

The entryway argument was rewritten a third time after reading the Greek of Sophistici Elenchi 183b to 184b rather than the excerpt, which showed four supports for the conventional account that the entry had not credited: Aristotle draws the art-versus-products distinction himself with the shoemaker who hands out shoes; his named comparison class is paid eristic teachers and Gorgias, not Plato; the contrast is with rhetoric's old written tradition; and Prior Analytics I.31 supplies retrospective subsumption in its own words, the dividers not understanding. Three overstatements were withdrawn. What survives is a question the conventional account has never had to answer: whether a predecessor can possess a general, named, repeatable method which Aristotle calls a part of his own, while Aristotle truthfully says no part of it was previously worked out.

The ancient commentators made the same linkage. Philoponus glosses I.31 with no one of those before us knew this, and Alexander takes the target to include Plato, so the two passages were read together in antiquity.

The paper took its architecture and its title: MANY AND ONE, six stations across twelve positions, ending on a symmetrical pair rather than a verdict — what observation requires the extra maker, and what external observation forbids the single maker.

And the session's own failure mode is named in it. Four times the tradition's own product was supplied as external evidence; twice source criticism was filed in the measurements register; and once a number that did not measure the variable was announced as a refutation, which is the same fabrication as announcing a success, with rigour worn as costume.
